stemBlocks.value: Make x the subject of the formula y = mx + c.
Think first: Two operations act on x — multiplication by m and addition of c — so undo them in reverse order.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p055-q06 from workbook page 55.

solutionSteps.instruction: Identify the operations acting on x.

contentBlocks.value: x is multiplied by m, then c is added
undo the multiplication, valid for m ≠ 0

strategyBlocks.value: Subtract c from both sides, then divide both sides by m.

whyThisWorks.value: When more than one operation acts on the wanted letter, they must be undone in the opposite order to which they were applied — the addition of c is removed before the multiplication by m. Dividing the whole of y − c by m, rather than just the y, is essential because m multiplies x alone and so must divide the entire remaining side. This rearrangement is the standard way of reading an x-value off the straight-line equation y = mx + c.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing x = y − c/m, which divides only the c by m.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing x = y − c/m, which divides only the c by m.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing by m before subtracting c.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing by m before subtracting c.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing x = (y + c)/m by moving c across without changing its sign.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing x = (y + c)/m by moving c across without changing its sign.

examTip.value: Once you divide, put the whole numerator in brackets: (y − c)/m. That bracket is what stops the answer from being misread and is worth a mark on its own.
